children.value: > Fact From Story A new class action lawsuit filed this week in the U.S. District Court in D.C. accuses Google and parent company Alphabet of anticompetitive behavior in violation of U.S. antitrust law, the Sherman Act, and others, on behalf of news publishers.

> > Fact From Story In the complaint, Helena World Chronicle, which owns and publishes two weekly newspapers in Arkansas, argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.”
> > > Fact From Story It also specifically cites new AI technologies like Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot as worsening the problem.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge AI technologies can significantly impact the way information is accessed and consumed.

> > Fact From Story The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > > Fact From Story The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Question-and-answer technologies can draw information from various sources.
> > Commonsense Knowledge A company starving the free press and siphoning off content is anticompetitive behavior.
> Commonsense Knowledge A lawsuit is a legal proceeding brought by one party against another alleging a wrong or violation of rights.
